name: Sicanian

ancestors.notes: The handful of surviving short Sicanian inscriptions use the Greek alphabet under contact with Greek colonists; even the existence of Sicanian as a language distinct from Sicel or Elymian is open to question (Tribulato 2012, pp. 164-166).

notes: Stub: no citable grapheme-to-IPA inventory, and no established genetic classification. Extinct language (or dialect continuum) of pre-Greek western/central Sicily; Wikipedia states plainly that 'the language is unclassified due to lack of data'. Only a few short Greek-alphabet inscriptions survive and, apart from names, they remain untranslated. No `parent` is asserted because no genetic affiliation is established in the literature (an isolate/unclassified override via `family` is used instead, per SCHEMA.md); graphemes is left empty because no grapheme-to-sound correspondence has been proposed for the untranslated corpus.

sources.author: Tribulato, Olga
